ambiguities.description: The objectives are stated as goals without measurable acceptance criteria (e.g. "streamlined", "effectively"), so a bidder cannot tell what level of performance or functionality will be judged compliant; the bidder would ask what specific capabilities or metrics must be demonstrated for each objective.

The text lists the City's current modules and notes "Currently, five users" but does not state whether the new system must support only five users or a different number, nor whether data migration from the Tyler Fund Balance system is required; the bidder would ask for the required user count and migration scope.

The text refers to "any attachments" and "any addenda" without naming them, so a bidder cannot tell which documents are currently in force or how many there are; the bidder would ask for a list of the attachments and addenda issued to date.

The schedule says the Contract Lead will make every effort to adhere to it, so it is unclear whether these dates are firm deadlines or targets; a bidder would ask whether the proposal submission date of August 28, 2025 is a hard deadline and whether late proposals are rejected.

The RFP does not define what qualifies as a trade secret or how the City will treat marked information, yet marking implies the respondent has made that determination; a bidder would ask what criteria the City applies and what happens if a marking is disputed.

The City's standard contract with terms and conditions is only "available upon request" and is not included in this chunk, so the bidder cannot know the terms it must accept before the question deadline; the bidder would ask for a copy of the standard contract and when it will be provided.

The City states it may "leave open the possibility for later negotiation and amendment of specific contract provisions" while also rejecting any modified terms submitted with a proposal; it is unclear which provisions are negotiable and through what mechanism, which affects how the bidder frames exceptions.

The text directs bidders to the question period "in accordance with the instructions in Section 2.3" but does not state the question deadline or submission channel here; a bidder would ask for the exact question-period dates and how proposed modifications must be submitted.

The text allows exceptions for "general inquiries before submission and after status updates" but does not define who may be contacted or what counts as a general inquiry, so a bidder cannot tell which pre-submission contacts are safe; the bidder would ask which contact point and topics are permitted.

The disqualification exception turns on the City's subjective judgment that a communication was "harmless and unintentional" and in the City's best interest, with no process for raising or curing a possible violation; the bidder would ask whether a cure or clarification procedure exists.

The City may reject any proposal on the basis of "fit, form, and function" without defining those terms, so a bidder cannot tell what would make a proposal unacceptable beyond cost and stated specifications; the bidder would ask what criteria define fit, form and function.

The criterion "Technical support during software implementation and ongoing" is truncated and does not say what level or duration of ongoing support is expected, so bidders cannot scope or price it; the bidder would ask what support scope, hours and term are required.

The text says submissions deemed noncompliant or technically unqualified will not be considered but does not define what makes a submission noncompliant; the bidder would ask which mandatory requirements cause disqualification.

The text says no single requirement automatically disqualifies a respondent, yet non-compliance with any individual requirement may lead the City to reject a proposal entirely; a bidder would ask which requirements are pass/fail and how partial compliance is scored.

The page limit is stated as "should not exceed 20 pages" (desired) while the surrounding text says respondents are "required to adhere" to the guidelines; a bidder would ask whether exceeding 20 pages (plus allowances) makes a proposal non-responsive.

The hard copy must be "received" by the deadline, but the text does not state whether the 4:00 PM PST deadline applies to physical delivery as well as the email; a bidder would ask what time the hard copy must arrive and whether a postmark suffices.
The text refers to a proposal opening time "stated on the cover page", but the cover page is not part of this chunk, so the bidder cannot confirm the exact withdrawal cutoff from this text alone.
"Good cause" for post-opening withdrawal is undefined and left to City discretion; a bidder would ask what circumstances qualify.

The text refers to "the required elements outlined below" and "additional details required for each proposal section" that are not contained in this chunk, so a bidder cannot tell from this text which sections and elements are mandatory; the bidder would ask for the complete list of required proposal elements.

It is unclear who qualifies as an "authorized signature" (e.g., an officer, a specific title, or a person holding a power of attorney) and whether notarization is needed; the bidder would ask what signatory authority must be documented.

The list of "Specific elements of the RFP response" is introduced without a shall/must, so it is unclear whether these five items are mandatory contents of Tab 1 or merely suggested; a bidder would ask whether omitting any of them makes the response non-responsive.

The proposal goals and the deliverables are referenced only by cross-reference to Section 5.0, which is not included in this chunk; a bidder would ask which goals and deliverables must be addressed in Tab 1.

The July 1, 2026 go-live is stated as the City's "goal" rather than a contractual milestone, so it is unclear whether the implementation timeline is a firm commitment with penalties or an aspirational target the Respondent should plan toward.

The text does not define what the "levels of support" and "license levels" are (e.g., tiers, SLAs, hours of coverage), so a bidder cannot tell whether to propose its own tier structure or respond to a City-defined one.

The chunk refers to "this information" without defining what firm information and qualifications must be provided for each team member; a bidder would ask what specific content is required per company.

The City expresses a "desire" for participation by minority-, women-, disabled- and small-business enterprises but sets no goal, percentage or required form of evidence, so a bidder cannot tell whether a specific subcontracting commitment or documentation is expected.

The text requires "recent experience" without defining a cutoff period, so a bidder cannot tell which past projects qualify; the bidder would ask how many years back counts as recent and how many references or projects must be listed.

"Local referral" is undefined (local to Colfax, to the county, or to the region), and it is unclear whether the referral must be a client reference or merely a contact able to host a demonstration; the bidder would ask what geographic area and relationship qualify.

The text requires reimbursable expenses to be capped but does not state a cap amount or whether the City sets one; a bidder would ask whether a maximum reimbursable amount or percentage is prescribed.

The text does not define what constitutes "similar services" for the three required references, so a bidder cannot tell whether references must match the full scope, a subset, or a comparable industry; the bidder would ask for the criteria.

The required insurance types are open-ended ("including, but not limited to") and no minimum coverage limits or additional-insured requirements are stated here, so the bidder cannot price the coverage; the bidder would ask what limits and coverages are required.

It is unclear what specific documentation or format satisfies Attachment G's demonstration of financial data protection and secure access controls (e.g., policies, certifications such as SOC 2, or a completed questionnaire).

The chunk refers to "required items" and "optional items" in the scope of work but does not identify which deliverables are which; a bidder would ask for the definitive list of required versus optional deliverables.

The scope does not define what "support" for the first 12 months post-implementation includes (hours, response times, channels, on-site vs remote), which drives staffing and price. The bidder would ask what service levels and coverage apply during that period.

The scope does not state which software system is being implemented or whether the vendor supplies, installs or merely assists with it, so the installation and data-import obligations are unclear. The bidder would ask what product/platform is in scope and who is responsible for installation.

The July 1, 2026 completion date is stated as a "goal" rather than a firm deadline, so it is unclear whether it is a binding milestone with consequences or an aspiration; the bidder would ask whether the date is contractually enforceable.

The project start is described only as "soon after awarding the contract and finalizing negotiations," leaving the start date and any notice period open; the bidder would ask for the expected award date or a defined start trigger to build the schedule.

The text requires a capped reimbursable expense amount but gives no cap level, ceiling or basis for setting it, so bidders cannot know whether their proposed cap will be acceptable; the bidder would ask whether the City has a maximum allowable cap or expects the respondent to propose one.

It is unclear how the three total figures (total price for services and deliverables, total reimbursable expenses cap, and total price proposal) relate, i.e. whether the total price proposal is the sum of the other two or a separate all-inclusive figure; the bidder would ask for the intended arithmetic.

The references must be for "similar services ... as outlined herein", but this chunk does not define what counts as similar; the bidder would ask what scope or service categories qualify as similar references.

The form requires written notice of relocation outside the United States but sets no timeframe or notice period; a bidder would ask how far in advance notice must be given and to whom it must be addressed.

The certification lists the same audit/unqualified-opinion statement twice as two separate checkboxes, so it is unclear whether both must be checked or whether one is a duplicate; the bidder would ask which boxes are required.

The text does not say how or to whom the 15-day change notification must be delivered (form, channel, address), and 'material changes' is undefined; the bidder would ask what notification method and threshold apply.

The required coverage limits, additional-insured status and certificate form for the workers compensation and commercial general liability policies are not stated, so the bidder cannot price the insurance or know whether its current coverage qualifies; the bidder would ask what limits and endorsements are required.

The text does not specify what form or level of detail the documentation of financial-data protection and access controls must take (e.g., policies, certifications, diagrams), nor whether it is a narrative response or an attached artifact; a bidder would ask what format and evidence are expected.
Conflicting requirements R040 and R044: R040 requires a signed hard-copy original proposal while R044 requires the proposal and all attachments to be emailed, giving incompatible submission methods.

Conflicting requirements R097 and R137: R097 requires notice to the City within 30 days of material changes to the financial certification, while R137 requires notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days for the same changes.
